title: ReEmBody: Relationship, Emotion, and Body Experience, and Their Link with Sexuality
summary: Binge-eating can contribute to overweight and obesity and is co-determined by psychological factors. Sexual experience and body image are frequently impaired in both obesity and eating disorders. To design adequate treatments, these factors and connections need to be better understood. This study examines relationships between sexuality and relevant psychological factors in obese women with binge-eating behavior. The study investigates: (1) how they experience and use their bodies, and how this relates to their sexual experience and sexual difficulties, (2) which emotions they express facially when talking about their body and sexuality, and (3) how their vocal rhythm coordinates with that of the interviewing person as a measure of implicit interaction behavior. We conduct psychodynamic interviews about body image and sexuality and analyze the video and audio recordings as well as interview transcripts. Using subsequently collected questionnaire data, results from these methods not previously used in this patient group shall be related to those of validated measurement instruments, including with regard to personality structure.

interventions.name: Observational Group: Obese women (BMI > 30) with binge-eating behaviour
Normal-weight women (18 < BMI < 25) without current or past eating disorder

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•  Group 1: BMI > 30 and eating disorder diagnosis with binge-eating behavior (ICD-10 F50.8/.9) 
•  Group 2: 18 < BMI < 25 and no current mental illness
Exclusion criteria:
Insufficient German language skills; pregnancy within the last two years or breastfeeding; neurological disorders affecting facial expression; facial procedures or conditions affecting facial muscle function; medications significantly affecting facial muscle function; acute psychiatric crisis; active substance use disorders; severe cardiovascular diseases; acute metabolic disorders
